_readme: Three-check audit of content/guides/*.json, 5 a night.

changed: Magadha capital: Rajagriha first, later Pataliputra
Ashoka's reign 268 to 232 BCE: added 'scholars differ by a few years'
Ashoka's edicts: 'earliest securely dated, deciphered' records (body and FAQ)
Nalanda 'continued', Vikramashila 'flourished' under the Palas
Mesolithic table row: from about 12,000 years ago, later in some regions
Harappan: 'most extensive of the early Bronze Age urban civilisations' (was 'largest')
UPSC FAQ: Prelims history of India; Mains GS I culture from ancient to modern times (Mains has no ancient-history item)
unconfirmed_recheck: Megasthenes/Faxian/Xuanzang: verifier 2 tools blocked; verifier 3 found them standing

changed: Indus inscriptions: 'on average about five signs' (Mahadevan), was 'most have fewer than six'
Indus non-linguistic view: 'many specialists dispute', was 'most specialists reject'
Kharosthi in use until about the 4th or 5th century CE (body, table, FAQ; Britannica)
Gandharan birch-bark manuscripts dated about 1st century BCE to 2nd century CE (was 'around 1st century CE')
Grantha from about the 5th or 6th century CE (body, table)
Nagari table: from about the 7th or 8th century CE
'nearly every indigenous Indian script' descends from Brahmi (body, social caption)
unconfirmed_recheck: Siddham in East Asia: verifier 2 tools blocked; verifier 3 found them standing (Salomon 1998)

changed: Calcutta University anthropology department: 1921, was 1920 (caluniv.ac.in)
AnSI: set up 1945, HQ in Kolkata since 1948 (began in Varanasi)
South India row: 'Nilgiri and other southern hill communities' (Soliga and Chenchu are not Nilgiri)
'Gond Pandvani' changed to 'the Pandvani of Chhattisgarh'
Bhopal Tribal Museum: tribal artists made the displays (was 'helped design the galleries')
unconfirmed_recheck: university list: verifier 2 tools blocked; verifier 3 found them standing

changed: Paper II bullet: the syllabus does not name the Fifth/Sixth Schedules or PESA; now 'history of tribal policies and development programmes, constitutional safeguards, forest policy and welfare programmes'
FAQ GS overlap: 'related themes ... constitutional provisions' (GS syllabus does not name the Schedules or forest rights)
unconfirmed_recheck: 250 marks x 2, 3 hours, free choice of optional: upsc.gov.in blocked for verifier 2; verifier 3 confirmed from CSE rules; re-read the official notification

changed: Blue board: 'usually carry a board' (no source for 'blue' or 'every'; CAG found signage gaps), also social hook, caption, reel
Social hook 'older than most Indian railways' replaced with 'The ASI has been at work since 1861.'
Survey 'wound up in 1866', was 'suspended for a few years' (ASI history)
unconfirmed_recheck: Superintending Archaeologists head circles; Hampi is a mini circle

changed: Indian Institute of Heritage named as the deemed university formerly called the National Museum Institute (IIH notices; ThePrint 20 Apr 2026)
PG Diploma kept as one year: ThePrint 20 Apr 2026 reports it was cut from two years to one
'Some universities' replaces 'a few universities' in FAQ
held: 'Very few universities offer a BA in archaeology alone' removed: no source counts them
University of Delhi removed from list of archaeology departments: no archaeology department found

changed: 'Written records' now 'securely dated, readable written records' begin with Ashoka
Cunningham 'published' (not collected) the Harappa seal (ASR vol. 5, 1875)
Antiquities Act 1972: export barred except by the Central Government or an authorised agency (s.3), was 'without a licence'
Excavation 'needs official permission' (licence strictly for protected areas)
Social hook 'a thousand years of history' replaced with 'the inscriptions of early India'
held: 'Pushed back by some two thousand years' softened to 'many centuries': sources disagree on the figure
Sarnath dropped from Cunningham's identifications: ASI history names Sankisa, Sravasti, Kausambi
'through its Central Advisory Board of Archaeology' removed: not confirmed in the Rules
FAQ: William Jones as 'father of Indian archaeology' removed: no reputable source
FAQ: 'Hampi one of the largest historic city sites' removed: UNESCO gives area only

changed: Taxila: 'sent to Taxila' (Ashokavadana), not governor
Pillar edicts: six at most sites, all seven only at Delhi-Topra (Hultzsch CII 1)
Rest houses attributed to Pillar Edict 7, not Rock Edict 2
Prinsep sentence no longer says he used the edicts 'largely' (he used Sanchi donor inscriptions)
Delhi-Topra 'set up in his citadel' (was 'on top of his palace'); Delhi-Meerut 'on the Ridge in north Delhi' (Hindu Rao detail lightly sourced)
Reel line: 'over 2,200 years old' (was 2,250)
FAQ: National Museum has 'a major Harappan gallery' (was 'the largest in India', unsourced)
Name 'traditionally traced' to Buddhist and Jain script lists
'about forty basic signs' now 'a small set of basic signs' (count depends on method)
Devanagari FAQ: date 'end of first millennium CE' dropped
held: Kodumanal removed from pre-Ashokan potsherd sites: not confirmed by checker A

changed: Four-field model now 'associated with Franz Boas and American anthropology' (early 20th century dating dropped)
Karla chaitya dated 'around the turn of the Common Era' (Britannica late 1st c BCE vs Dehejia 1st c CE)
Ajanta later phase now 5th to 6th c CE, linked with the Vakatakas (UNESCO); 'horseshoe bend' wording replaced
Udayagiri (Vidisha) caves 'mostly Hindu'
FAQ: early caves 'around the 2nd and 1st centuries BCE'
held: 'Well over a thousand rock-cut caves in Maharashtra' removed: no acceptable source; now 'hundreds'

changed: Thanjavur vimana now 'about 60 metres' (UNESCO 59.82 m; 66 m unsupported)
Reigns softened: Vijayalaya to about 870, Parantaka I to the mid-950s, Rajaraja I/Rajendra I about 1014 (UNESCO 1012 vs Britannica 1014)
Gangaikonda Cholapuram capital 'in the 1020s'; Srivijaya raid 'known from his inscriptions'
Decline dated to the 13th century (Britannica: Hoysalas from 1216, Pandyas 1257)
Natya Shastra dated 'about the 2nd century BCE to the 3rd century CE' (Britannica range)
held: 'Ministry of Culture has listed Chhau' removed: no government source found; now 'some books also count Chhau'

changed: Pali and Prakrit 'like Sanskrit' not the main language of any state (Sanskrit was wrongly excluded)
Expert committee named: set up by Ministry of Culture under Sahitya Akademi (pmindia.gov.in)
Sanskrit tradition 'about three thousand years'
